extracted.intended_audience: Visual artists, writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary and performance artists, and collaborative teams applying for the Ucross artist residency
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and program requirements for artists applying to the Ucross Foundation residency program (two sessions per year) including eligibility, deadlines, residency length, amenities, and applicant responsibilities. Intended to inform prospective applicants what to expect and when/how to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: The residency program is open to visual artists, writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary artists, performance artists, and collaborative teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from all those listed disciplines may apply; collaborative teams are explicitly permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional standing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must exhibit professional standing in their field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both established and emerging artists are encouraged to apply — the program looks for evidence of professional engagement in the applicant's discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency length
rubrics_metrics.description: Residencies range from two weeks to six weeks in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should plan projects that fit within this 2–6 week window; the program schedules residencies within two yearly sessions (Fall and Spring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Session schedule and application windows
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two residency sessions each year: Fall (August through early December) and Spring (February through early June).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open call periods: Fall open call runs November 1 to January 15; Spring open call runs May 1 to July 15. Example specific deadline: the Spring 2027 session application deadline is July 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. MT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency capacity and typical discipline mix
rubrics_metrics.description: At any one time there are up to ten individuals in residence; each year the program provides residencies to approximately 115 individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical at-a-time breakdown is four writers, four visual artists, and two composers — applicants should be aware of the program's cohort size and typical disciplinary balance when applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program amenities and living conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ucross provides each artist with living accommodations, meals, work space, and uninterrupted time so that the artists can focus on their creative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: lunch and dinners are prepared Monday to Friday by a professional chef; lunches are delivered to individual studios; group dinners take place at 6 p.m.; towels and all linens are provided; weekly housekeeping for bedrooms; there is cell phone service and wireless internet throughout residency facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibilities (materials & travel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Residents are responsible for providing their own working materials and for their travel to Sheridan, Wyoming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no charge for a residency — applicants should budget for travel and materials but not residency fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program mission and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ucross strives to provide a respectful, comfortable, and productive environment, freeing artists from the pressures and distractions of daily life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program emphasizes uninterrupted time and the connections built within the community; applicants should propose work that can make meaningful use of solitude and community interaction provided by the residency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized fellowships and alternative residencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Ucross offers dedicated Fellowships for Native American Visual Artists and Writers and also runs a Culinary Residency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who are Native American artists or who are interested in the Culinary Residency should consult the dedicated fellowship/residency pages for additional, program-specific criteria and application instructions.
